sections.title: Progressive Skill Discovery as Access Control for Tool-Using LLM Agents: Structural Governance through Role-Scoped Capability Delivery
sections.abstract: The paper introduces skilder, which exposes tools to an LLM agent only through task-discovered, role-scoped skills and reports no unauthorized tool calls or parameter violations in its governed-call evaluation.
sections.claimed_contribution: Role-scoped capability delivery combines deterministic governance boundaries with dynamic cross-role capability acquisition.
sections.caveat: The evidence is a six-model, 13-task evaluation and task-pass misses include discovery and response-quality failures.

sections.title: DEEPO: Dual-Entropy Enhanced Policy Optimization for Hallucination in MLLMs
sections.abstract: DEEPO combines entropy-triggered expert prefixes with advantage-sign-aware Renyi preconditioning to improve reinforcement-learning correction of hallucinations in multimodal language models.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report a statistically significant +4.0 percentage-point interaction gain on VideoMMMU and additive gains elsewhere.
sections.caveat: Transfer beyond the evaluated multimodal tasks and training setup remains unestablished.

sections.title: SLCA-GRPO: Resolving Cross-Segment Credit Misattribution in Tool-Calling RL
sections.abstract: SLCA-GRPO assigns separate execution and preference advantages to tool-call and summary segments, using a schema-guided simulator.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report gains over GRPO, ToolPO, and RLTR on in-domain, BFCL, and tau-squared-Bench evaluations.
sections.caveat: Results rely on a simulator and selected benchmarks; real-API transfer remains open.

sections.title: Where Does Exactly-Once Live? Model, Harness, and Tool-Contract Effects on Duplicate Side Effects in LLM Agents
sections.abstract: LIMBO evaluates duplicate side effects under realistic failures and finds that exactly-once behavior depends on the fault, with idempotency keys outperforming waiting or verification alone.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper reports idempotency keys reduce duplicate writes from 28% to 4% in its setting.
sections.caveat: Conclusions are tied to LIMBO's services, fault model, contracts, models, and recovery conditions.

sections.title: Synthetic Hospital: An Open, Verifiable, Physician-Validated Longitudinal EHR Benchmark
sections.abstract: Synthetic Hospital provides 1,268 synthetic longitudinal patients and 5,602 encounters grounded in medical ontologies and provenance.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report near-chance physician discrimination from real charts and a best-model severity-weighted F1 of 0.73.
sections.caveat: Synthetic records require further validation against protected real-world EHR distributions.

sections.title: IterSynth: Rethinking Deep Search Agents via Role-Decoupled Iterative Synthesis
sections.abstract: IterSynth separates planning from evidence synthesis and keeps an evolving summary as search state, while RDPO supplies role-specific reinforcement-learning credit assignment.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report IterSynth-8B average score 50.7, +4.2% over the strongest prior <=8B agent.
sections.caveat: The abstract does not isolate all contributions outside the reported ablations.

sections.title: ELF-REG: Scaling Continuous Diffusion Language Models to Reasoning Tasks
sections.abstract: ELF-REG uses representation alignment and entanglement with a frozen autoregressive teacher to improve fully continuous diffusion language models on math and code tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper reports 55.96% GSM8K pass@1 at 64 NFE and improves MATH-500 from 10.55% to 13.39% over its baseline.
sections.caveat: The abstract does not show parity with leading autoregressive systems.

sections.title: PROOF: Profiling Reliability of Object-Level Facts in Large Language Models
sections.abstract: PROOF profiles factual coverage across facts, relations, domains, prompt formulations, and decoding perturbations rather than reducing reliability to one aggregate score.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report large domain and formulation sensitivities, including up to 26.5 percentage points from wording changes.
sections.caveat: The benchmark uses a frozen Wikidata snapshot and controlled prompts.
